You will be joining a team whose primary mission is solving the intricate enigma of securing and innovating the boot process for our GPUs, while working through the formidable constraints of boot-time and storage space. Every. Byte. Counts. 


The GPU Firmware team builds the root of trust firmware for GPUs that provides secure boot, update, and attestation services for all our GPU products from gaming to high-performance compute in the datacenter. We want your help to build an industry leading security posture for a security critical component across all these products. 

What you’ll be doing: 

  • Design, develop, test, debug, and optimize GPU firmware throughout the entire GPU lifecycle 
  • Continuously evaluate and improve the security posture of firmware and hardware that form the root of trust for our products 
  • Improve team software process and core infrastructure by enhancing build systems, regression farms, and security test infrastructure 
  • Participate in in-depth security reviews of software, hardware, process, and infrastructure 
  • Facilitate security requirements and solutions by participating in industry standards such as NIST, Open Compute Project, DMTF etc., and aligning with key customers and partners 
  • Collaborate with NVIDIA’s and third-party vendors’ hardware and software teams to improve security across hardware, BootROMs, and software stacks 
  • Work within a larger virtual security team on other parts of the GPU stack, as necessary 

What we need to see: 

  • BS or MS degree in EE/CS/CE (or equivalent experience)
  • 5+ years’ experience in developing device BIOS, firmware, or other low-level software 
  • 2+ years’ experience in building secure firmware and working with hardware security components 
  • Strong C skills 
  • Secure software fundamentals including cryptography, authentication/attestation, chains of trust, and understanding of common SW security vulnerabilities 
  • Easy to work with, as you’ll constantly work closely with both hardware designers and other software engineers to design, develop, and debug functional (and non-functional!) aspects of GPU subsystems 

Ways to stand out from the crowd: 

  • Experience with threat modeling, formal design analysis, hardware/firmware architecture, and other demonstrable security experience in a defensive security focused role. 
  • Background with secure development techniques such as attack-trees, static/dynamic analysis, fuzzing, and negative testing 
  • Experience developing for safety critical platforms

descriptionHtml:

title: Director, Forward Deployed Engineering - Open Models
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to help the world build custom AI at scale? We’re hiring a founding Director to build and lead NVIDIA’s Forward Deployed Engineering organization for open models, including NVIDIA Nemotron and NVIDIA Cosmos, across North America. The mission is to turn open models into production-ready AI tuned to a specific domain, delivered through our partner ecosystem. We want any organization to build, own, and run its own AI on open source models, and this organization helps the ecosystem get there!


Unlike most forward deployed organizations, ours works primarily through NVIDIA’s partner ecosystem. Our FDEs work side by side with top partner engineering and research teams, co-lead joint customer engagements, and build the recipes and playbooks that help partners succeed and scale. This leader sets the strategy for North America, builds the organization, and carries the vision to partners, customers, and NVIDIA leadership. Are you an exceptional technical leader with deep roots in open model post-training and agent harness engineering, ready to build a world-class FDE organization? We’d love to meet you.


What you’ll be doing:

  • This role sets the strategy and leads the team that delivers custom AI to end customers through NVIDIA’s partner ecosystem. The team deepens partner relationships and leads three-way engagements among NVIDIA, the partner, and the end customer. Our goal is hundreds of end customers running domain-specific Nemotron or Cosmos in production, supported by a strong ecosystem that delivers it.
  • Hire and develop FDE leads, managers, and senior engineers across North America, and set a high bar for technical depth and customer impact. Create clear paths for growth and a team structure that scales with the ecosystem.
  • The work stays technical. Set the technical direction for post-training, evaluation, harness engineering, and inference optimization, and be the person the team turns to on the hardest engagements. Keep up with the open model, post-training, and agents landscape, and bring new use cases and partner opportunities forward before partners ask.
  • Partners are how we reach customers at scale. Build trusted relationships with leaders at partner and end-customer companies, shape joint plans and agreements, and see three-way engagements through to production. Set clear goals and track the results: partners adopting Nemotron, customers running in production, and customers willing to speak publicly. We help partners succeed on their own with reusable recipes, reference pipelines, and playbooks, so more developers can build domain-specific AI.
  • We connect NVIDIA’s model research to partner and customer use cases. Work with Product, Research, and Engineering to bring what we see in the field back into Nemotron, Cosmos, and our software stack, and share what works with FDE leaders in other regions. Align priorities and resources with sales, partner, and solutions leaders, keep senior leadership informed on progress, and speak on NVIDIA domain-specific open models.
  • Above all, we’re excited to help organizations worldwide build, own, and run their own AI on open source models!


What we need to see:

  • Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Computer Science, Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 14+ overall years in ML or software engineering, applied AI, FDE, or solutions architecture, including 8+ years leading technical teams and 5+ years of hands-on LLM post-training with models taken to production.
  • A track record of building and scaling technical organizations across multiple locations and time zones, including managing managers or leads, and setting goals and measuring results for a customer-facing technical team.
  • Deep technical credibility in post-training (LoRA/PEFT, SFT, and synchronous and asynchronous reinforcement learning), model architectures, synthetic data, and evaluation, plus agent harness engineering and optimization for LLM and agentic systems. Good understanding of large-scale distributed training and inference performance optimization across multi-GPU and multi-node systems.
  • Deep understanding of the partner, open model, and cloud provider ecosystem, and where NVIDIA can add the most value. Proven ability to build alignment across multiple partners and customers on the same engagement, including at the executive level. Good understanding of how to drive ecosystem demand and match partners with customers.
  • Proven ability to scope engagements, shape SOWs, and deliver consistently high quality across many engagements at once.
  • Clear communication of complex technical ideas, from engineers to C-level executives. Excellent judgment, prioritization, and organizational skills, and comfort leading through ambiguity. Travel to partner and customer sites and NVIDIA offices up to [25%].


Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:

  • Experience building and scaling an FDE, applied research, or solutions organization from an early stage.
  • History of building partner-led programs, ecosystems motions.
  • Hands-on experience with Nemotron, Cosmos, and other open models, as well as serverless and self-managed post-training platforms (such as the Tinker API) and open-source frameworks such as NVIDIA NeMo and Megatron.
  • A technical vision that influences product, engineering, and business decisions and drives production outcomes.
  • Experience with multimodal or world-foundation-model post-training, and running training jobs on large GPU clusters with SLURM or Kubernetes with a passion for using AI tools to improve how the team builds, delivers, and scales.

title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer, Open Models

The mission is to turn open models into production-ready AI tuned to a specific domain, from post-training through harness optimization. descriptionHtml:

Explore and prototype hybrid architectures combining world models, generative (e.g., diffusion, flow matching) models, and policy gradients for realistic and robust simulation.

  • Experience building large-scale training pipelines with temporal consistency and simulation data replay.
  • Publications or open-source contributions in RL, model-based control, or autonomous systems.

descriptionHtml:

Run regressions, debug and triage failures, and reproduce issues in simulation when needed to support root-cause analysis and resolution.

  • Investigate failures across RTL, verification infrastructure, C/C++ models, and RNM models, and collaborate with designers to resolve issues.

  • Hands-on experience with Cadence Palladium or a comparable hardware emulation platform, including environment bring-up, regression execution, failure triage, and debug.
  • Strong C/C++ programming skills, with experience developing verification models, test infrastructure, or hardware validation tests.
  • Strong SystemVerilog skills and experience building verification environments using UVM.
  • Experience with constrained-random stimulus, functional coverage, assertions, and coverage closure.
  • Strong debugging and analytical skills, including isolating emulation failures and reproducing issues in simulation.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Direct experience bringing up and debugging SerDes IP or subsystems on Cadence Palladium.
  • Experience adapting UVM testbenches, C/C++ models, and mixed-signal behavioral models for efficient emulation.
  • Experience developing SerDes RNM models and correlating their behavior with analog simulation results or silicon measurements.

descriptionHtml:

  • Review layout, netlist, and runset interactions to identify root causes and recommend fixes.

  • Improve physical verification flow quality, turnaround time, and automation.
  • Collaborate with methodology, CAD, and foundry-facing teams on rule interpretation and signoff quality.

What we need to see:

  • B.Sc. or M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or equivalent experience.
  • 2+ years of experience in physical verification, backend implementation, or VLSI signoff.
  • Strong understanding of DRC, LVS, antenna, and layout verification concepts.
  • Hands-on experience with tools such as Calibre, ICV, Pegasus, or equivalent physical verification tools.
  • Ability to debug verification issues across layout, extracted views, and netlist connectivity.
  • Scripting ability in Tcl, Perl, Python, or shell for automation and debug.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Familiarity with stream-out/OASIS or GDSII generation and tapeout readiness flows.

title: Senior Research Scientist, AI-Enabled Secure Systems
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Senior Research Scientist to lead research on using AI to design, analyze, implement, and verify secure computer systems. The work spans hardware architectures, firmware, operating systems, runtimes, compilers, libraries, and applications, combining advances in generative AI and agents with program analysis, formal methods, synthesis, computer architecture, and software engineering.


The goal is to make security a property that can be designed and verified from the outset rather than added after deployment. You will create AI-enabled techniques that help researchers and engineers express security requirements, explore designs, identify flaws, generate secure implementations, construct or check proofs, and produce trustworthy hardware and software artifacts at practical scale. NVIDIA is a leader in accelerated computing and AI systems. This role offers the opportunity to set research direction, influence future platforms, and translate foundational advances into practical capabilities in collaboration with research, product, and engineering teams.


What you'll be doing:

  • Define a high-impact research agenda and lead projects in AI-enabled secure system design, implementation, analysis, and verification.
  • Develop models, agents, and tools for security requirements and specification, threat modeling, architecture exploration, secure code and hardware generation, program analysis, synthesis, and proof construction.
  • Combine AI techniques with static and dynamic analysis, formal verification, symbolic reasoning, testing, and domain-specific security knowledge to produce reliable and machine-checkable results.
  • Build end-to-end prototypes and evaluate them on realistic hardware and software systems, measuring security, correctness, scalability, performance, and human productivity.
  • Collaborate across hardware, software, AI, research, and product teams; publish original research; mentor researchers and interns; and translate advances into practical developer and design capabilities.

What we need to see:

  • A Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent research experience.
  • 6+ years of relevant experience, with an established record of research excellence demonstrated through influential publications, open-source systems, patents, technology transfer, or substantial research collaborations.
  • Deep expertise in one or more relevant areas such as formal methods, program analysis, programming languages, software or hardware security, computer architecture, compilers, AI for code, or automated reasoning and synthesis.
  • Experience defining and leading ambiguous, multi-disciplinary research projects and providing technical mentorship.
  • Strong implementation and experimental skills in C, C++, Python, hardware description languages, theorem provers, analysis frameworks, or relevant AI/ML tooling.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to connect foundational research with real engineering and product needs.

We are looking for a creative, collaborative, and self-directed researcher who wants to use AI to change how secure computer systems are conceived, built, and verified.

title: Math Device Extension Libraries Intern - 2027
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for software engineering interns to help us expand our catalog of Device eXtension (Dx) APIs for our math libraries. For over a decade, NVIDIA's accelerated computing platform has revolutionized HPC and AI with applications ranging from COVID-19 research to autonomous machines. Our team develops the GPU-accelerated mathematical libraries that make all of this possible.


The hardware and software accelerated computing ecosystem is constantly evolving, including shifts towards hybrid backends, deep integration with high-level languages and ecosystems (such as Python, Numpy, JAX, MLIR…), and optimization at runtime for maximum flexibility and performance. Our Dx APIs allow developers to embed highly-optimized mathematical operations in their applications for these and other scenarios. You will be part of a team designing, developing, and optimizing math libraries for the future. Does the idea of being at the heart of these projects and applying your knowledge to develop and optimize algorithms which make an impact around world excite you? If yes, then come and join our team! During your internship, you will work with senior software engineers on the libraries team who will provide mentorship and guide you in developing highly optimized algorithms. Projects will involve implementing new numerical algorithms, defining APIs, analyzing performance, performance optimizations on the latest NVIDIA GPUs, improving libraries customer experience in employing agentic workflows and AI tools for their development and other general software engineering work.


What you'll be doing:

  • Prototype and develop numerical algorithms for high-performance math device extension libraries: cuBLASDx, cuSolverDx, cuFFTDx, cuRANDDx, nvCOMPDx, NPPDx or libmathdx on ground breaking NVIDIA graphics processors.
  • Analyze the performance of GPU implementations and find opportunities for improvements
  • Collaborate with team members to understand software use cases and requirements
  • Prototype tooling and solutions to help transform math libraries’ APIs into LLM-friendly representations across popular codegen tools.

What we need to see:

  • Pursuing a MS or PhD degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Applied Mathematics, or related field
  • Strong C++ programming, debugging, performance analysis, and test building skills
  • Parallel or GPU programming experience using CUDA, OpenMP, OpenCL, SYCL or similar
  • Experience with linear algebra or FFT or data compression algorithms

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

title: Senior Systems Software Engineer, Workload Systems Engineering
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is seeking a senior systems software engineer to help engineering teams run demanding build, simulation, and validation workloads efficiently and reliably. Our Workload Systems Engineering team connects customer workflows with the infrastructure that performs them. We develop self-service mechanisms and clear diagnostics, investigate performance and reliability across system boundaries, and deliver measured infrastructure improvements with the teams that own the underlying components.


Your responsibilities include enabling application configuration, remote execution, workers, hosts, GPU and CPU resources, storage, data paths, and on-target systems. The position requires direct system evaluation: diagnosing causes of slow or failing workloads, trying alternatives in representative scenarios, applying improvements with others, and verifying customer advantages.


What you'll be doing:

  • Build shared self-service and validation mechanisms that let engineering teams configure and use supported infrastructure workflows with less manual assistance.
  • Give customers and on-call teams useful diagnostic views across application, submission, remote-execution, and host or target layers so they can identify where failures and slowdowns originate.
  • Set performance and reliability benchmarks for representative workloads. Apply profiling, metrics, traces, and controlled experiments to pinpoint the changes that make a difference.
  • Evaluate and improve compute and GPU selection, scheduling and placement, concurrency, worker and runner configuration, resource sharing, caching, and input/output paths.
  • Make retry causes, recovery outcomes, and wasted execution capacity visible. Work with component owners to eliminate recurring failures and unnecessary re-execution.
  • Implement and validate infrastructure-level changes with application, build and CI, remote-execution, and infrastructure teams. Measure the effect on turnaround, successful efficiency, stability, usable capacity, and cost.
  • Turn successful investigations into supported workflows, diagnostics, documentation, and clear customer handoffs.

What we need to see:

  • Over 8 years of solid software engineering experience working with production compute infrastructure, distributed systems, large-scale build and test systems, or comparable systems software.
  • Hands-on experience debugging complex performance or reliability issues across software and hardware boundaries using logs, metrics, traces, profiling, and experiments.
  • Proficiency in a systems programming or automation language and experience delivering tested changes into production infrastructure.
  • In-depth experience with Linux and proficiency in one or more of these fields: GPU systems and drivers, scheduling and resource management, remote execution or CI infrastructure, storage and data paths, or host and container infrastructure.
  • Ability to work across teams with different component ownership, turn ambiguous symptoms into a clear technical plan, and explain results to engineering customers.
  • A degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience with GPU sharing and isolation, CUDA execution behavior, MIG or MPS or equivalent experience, GPU driver diagnostics, or high-performance computing workloads.
  • Experience with workload placement, CPU and GPU concurrency, NUMA, cloud-instance benchmarking, or cost and performance tradeoffs.
  • Familiarity with Bazel, remote execution, build front ends, simulation or replay workloads, and hardware-in-the-loop validation.
  • Experience improving file-system, caching, networking, or high-throughput data paths under concurrent workloads.
  • A record of building customer self-service or observability tools and using incident and retry data to drive verified reliability improvements.

title: AI Research Scientist
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is searching for outstanding AI researchers to join the NVIDIA Research Korea team. Our mission is to advance the frontiers of foundation models and agentic AI through data-centric research. We focus on developing more capable, efficient, and self-improving AI systems by improving how models learn from data, spanning pre-training, post-training, and inference-time scaling. Our research explores synthetic data generation, data selection and curation, data-efficient learning, agentic reasoning, and iterative self-improvement.


A broader goal of our research is to advance Sovereign AI by developing generalizable methods and reproducible recipes that enable countries and language communities to build advanced AI systems without relying on massive amounts of human-annotated data. Building on NVIDIA Nemotron open models, we aim to make cutting-edge foundation models and agentic AI capabilities more accessible across languages, regions, and applications.

You will join a highly collaborative research team tackling fundamental challenges in foundation models and agentic AI. Our team aims to conduct groundbreaking research, contribute to the open-source AI ecosystem, and translate research innovations into NVIDIA technologies and products.


What you'll be doing:

  • Conduct cutting-edge research in foundation models and agentic AI, including reasoning, planning, tool use, and autonomous problem-solving.
  • Develop novel methods for data-efficient learning, data curation, and scalable model training for both pre-training and post-training.
  • Explore self-improvement techniques, including RL, distillation, self-training, and learning from model-generated feedback.
  • Advance the capabilities and efficiency of foundation models and agentic systems through innovative pre-training, post-training, and inference-time methods.
  • Develop advanced Korean-language foundation models and agentic systems, establishing methods and training recipes that generalize to other languages and regions.
  • Publish original research at leading conferences and contribute to open-source research.
  • Collaborate with researchers across NVIDIA and external academic institutions.
  • Mentor research interns from the NVIDIA-KAIST Joint AI Research Lab and contribute to a collaborative research environment with KAIST.
  • Present research findings at conferences, workshops, and other scientific events.
  • Transfer research innovations to NVIDIA product teams.

What we need to see:

  • PhD in AI, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
  • At least 4 years of relevant research experience.
  • Strong expertise in one or more of the following areas: LLMs, pre-training, agentic AI, reasoning, reinforcement learning, efficient model training, synthetic data generation, data-efficient learning, distillation, or self-improving AI.
  • Publications at leading conferences such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, COLM, ACL, EMNLP, or CVPR.
  • Strong understanding of modern deep learning methods and foundation models.
  • Excellent programming skills in Python and experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch.
  • Ability to identify important research problems, develop novel approaches, and conduct rigorous empirical evaluations.
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to collaborate effectively across research teams.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Research contributions to state-of-the-art foundation models, agentic systems, reasoning models, or autonomous AI.
  • Experience with large-scale distributed pre-training, efficient post-training, or inference-time scaling.
  • Impactful contributions to Korean-language AI, multilingual foundation models, or cross-lingual transfer.
  • Significant open-source contributions to foundation models, datasets, or agentic AI frameworks.

title: Silicon Product Engineer – Manufacturing
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA’s Silicon Co-Design Group sits at the crossroads of architecture, silicon, systems, and manufacturing, where first-principles thinking and engineering judgment at the highest level translate directly into product outcomes at scale. Our team gets every GPU, SoC, and CPU silicon program from first power-on to high-volume production.


We are hiring a Silicon Product Engineer – Manufacturing to join our Testability, Manufacturability, Reliability & Quality (TMRQ) team. You should have experience defining and validating SLT/BLT production coverage specifications on silicon and translating product requirements into effective test coverage that delivers quality, yield, and efficiency at scale. Hands-on lab experience with system-level post-silicon bring-up and silicon debugging is required. This role sits at the intersection of multi-functional HW/SW teams and Production Operations to make manufacturing an outstanding part of the overall Silicon co-design cycle, production release, and HVM testing! The exceptional hire continuously improves high-volume manufacturing workflows and products across functions and deliberately uses AI to drive impact while handling risk!


What you will be doing:

  • Responsible for developing and implementing robust closed-loop analysis for VF characteristics and POR expectations vs. production screens to improve overall quality of MFG screening diags.
  • Support VF/VMIN/VMAX/PVT spec validation and productization activities across Manufacturing teams and product segments.  
  • Partner multi-functionally with HW engineering teams such as Silicon PVT design and characterization teams, IO design and validation teams, system feature owners, SLT and BLT Production Operations, etc., to determine test coverage and constraints to resolve appropriate SLT/BLT test conditions, test content, and flows for high-volume manufacturing screens.
  • Support prototyping and fine-tune speed, power, circuits, yield, and quality for effective silicon coverage in the SLT socketed environment.
  • Support procedures to facilitate Silicon correlation activities between production testing infrastructure and internal Si characterization and diagnostics programs.
  • Coordinate, develop, and maintain SLT/BLT testing flows, incorporating takeaways from silicon and correlating them to design for shift-left improvements.
  • Initiate and drive process improvements and preventative actions through root cause analysis and data analytics.
  • Partner with SW and platform teams to support and improve SLT testing infrastructure, debug knobs, and data collection features needed to support manufacturing screens effectively.

What we need to see:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree or equivalent in Microelectronics/Electrical/Electronic/Computer Engineering or equivalent experience.
  • 3+ years of relevant industry experience in silicon Post-silicon PVT validation and/or high-volume manufacturing testing for complex SoCs, GPUs, CPUs, or similar.
  • Hands-on lab experience with silicon bring-up, lab debug, shmoo analysis, VF characteristics, test content bring-up, and correlation to Si characterization, yield, and coverage optimization.
  • Strong EE fundamentals, device physics, knowledgeable in Silicon design, statistics, STA concepts, fault analysis, sampling, and computer architecture.
  • Strong data analysis skills, a learning attitude, and prior experience working with large volumes of data.

title: System Software Engineer – Data Center GPU Compute Diagnostics
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. We are seeking a system software engineer to develop low-level diagnostic software for next-generation data center GPUs and rack-scale AI systems. Our team builds software that exercises and validates complex hardware, including compute engines, memory and cache subsystems, NICs, PCIe and NVLink interfaces, power delivery, and thermal behavior. This role is well suited to an embedded, firmware, device-driver, hardware-validation, or systems software engineer who enjoys working close to hardware. Relevant experience may come from GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage, servers, embedded systems, or other complex silicon-based products. Prior GPU, CUDA, or GEMM experience is helpful but not required; you will have the opportunity to learn GPU architecture and programming while working with experienced engineers. You will own well-scoped components of the diagnostic software from design through implementation, validation, productization, and field support. You will collaborate with hardware architects, driver developers, silicon-validation engineers, manufacturing teams, and field engineers to bring up new hardware and diagnose difficult system failures. Join an exciting, rewarding, and fast-moving environment building the systems that power modern AI.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Developing diagnostic and stress software in C/C++ and Python for complex hardware systems.
  • Interfacing with hardware blocks, firmware, Linux device drivers, registers, telemetry, and low-level debugging tools.
  • Bringing up and validating new silicon and system features using pre-production hardware and software.
  • Creating targeted tests for compute engines, memory and cache subsystems, DMA engines, PCIe/NVLink interfaces, power, and thermal behavior.
  • Investigating hardware and software failures involving memory errors, ECC, data integrity, performance, thermals, voltage/frequency behavior, and high-speed interfaces.
  • Contributing to diagnostic and stress workloads ranging from low-level tests for GPU hardware to higher-level AI workloads, with opportunities to develop expertise in CUDA programming, GEMM-style compute, NCCL, and PyTorch-based workloads.
  • Using modern development and analysis tools, including AI-assisted tools where appropriate, to accelerate coding, debugging, test creation, and failure analysis.

What we need to see:

  • BS or MS degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 2+ years of experience in embedded software, firmware, Linux device drivers, systems software, hardware validation, diagnostics, or silicon bring-up.
  • Strong programming skills in C and C++, plus working proficiency in Python.
  • Experience developing software that interacts with hardware, firmware, device drivers, hardware registers, or low-level interfaces.
  • Experience creating diagnostics, validation tests, stress tests, manufacturing tests, or other software used to isolate hardware or system failures.
  • Understanding of fundamental computer architecture concepts such as memory, caches, interrupts, DMA, buses, and device I/O.
  • Strong debugging and problem-solving skills, including the ability to investigate failures across hardware and software boundaries.
  • Ability to take ownership of a well-scoped problem and drive it to completion while collaborating with a technical lead and cross-functional teams.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills.

title: Senior System Software Engineer - Security
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA’s invention of the GPU in 1999 sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined modern computer graphics, and revolutionized parallel computing. GPU deep learning ignited the modern AI era — with NVIDIA hardware and software acting as the foundation for the world’s most ambitious AI, robotics, and autonomous systems workloads. NVIDIA is seeking a software engineer with systems software and security experience to join the Data Center Systems Software team. You will investigate and resolve product vulnerabilities and strengthen Secure Development Lifecycle (SDL) practices for platforms including HGX, DGX, and MGX. 


What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Investigate and reproduce vulnerabilities, assess exploitability and impact, and identify affected products and software versions. 
  • Assess third-party vulnerabilities and coordinate dependency updates, mitigations, or documented exceptions.

  • Build automation for vulnerability triage, analysis, and tracking. 
  • Improve SDL practices through threat modeling, security design reviews, and other best-practices. 
  • Evangelize and drive SDL practices across NVIDIA data center software teams. 

What We Need to See: 

  • BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience. 
  • 5+ years of relevant software or security engineering experience. 
  • Hands-on experience investigating and remediating vulnerabilities, including familiarity with CVSS scoring and CWE classification. 
  • Experience with secure development practices and security testing tools, such as static analysis, fuzzing, and software composition analysis. 
  • Familiarity with server firmware and systems software, plus experience building automation using Python or a comparable language. 
  • Experience with modern AI and Agents, including AI-forward mindset and proactive adoption of cutting-edge tools and techniques. 
  • The ability to drive resolution across distributed and diverse engineering teams. 
  • Solid technical foundation in embedded systems, with the ability to engage credibly in technical discussions around firmware architecture, memory safety, and hardware-software interfaces. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a strong preference for written communication that creates clarity and institutional memory for a remote team. 
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and complexity; you make sound decisions quickly with incomplete information and course-correct without friction. 

Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:

  • Develop detailed performance test plans to verify next-generation features.

  • Experience with EDA tools for simulation and debugging.
  • The ability to communicate technical status, risks, and trade-offs clearly to engineering leadership and cross-functional partners.

title: Senior Performance Research and Analysis Engineer
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA’s Performance Group is seeking a technical NIC & DPU Performance Research & Analysis Engineer to drive end-to-end performance strategy, characterization, optimization and HW offload accelerations for next-generation network interfaces and Data Processing Units (DPUs).

In this role, you will analyze and accelerate critical networking and storage technologies and protocols powering multi nodes AI clusters. You will profile performance across the complete hardware-to-software execution stack—stretching from DPU Arm CPU subsystems and PCIe to high-speed RDMA, SPDK, and DOCA acceleration pipelines.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Data-Path Optimization: Drive end-to-end benchmark plans, performance characterization, expectations and optimizations for NICs and DPUs deployed in distributed AI and cloud data centers.
  • Full-Stack Profiling: Profile low-level memory, PCIe, host CPU, and DPU ASIC execution paths to identify micro-architectural stragglers, queue bottlenecks, and tail-latency outliers.
  • Storage & Network Acceleration: Hands-on acceleration and offloading of storage (SPDK, NVMe-oF, VirtIO) and networking protocols (RDMA/RoCEv2, TCP/IP, DOCA).
  • AI-Assisted Workflow Automation: Leverage AI agents, autonomous scripts, and automated regression frameworks to scale continuous performance evaluation.
  • Cross-Functional RCA: Partner closely with Architecture, ASIC, Firmware, and Software engineering groups to conduct rigorous Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and establish performance targets for upcoming pre- and post-silicon platforms.

What We Need to See:

  • B.Sc. or M.Sc. in Computer Science, Computer/Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5+ years of experience in low-level networking, storage acceleration, and systems-level performance tuning in cloud or HPC environments.
  • Direct hands-on experience with at least two of the following: DOCA, SPDK, VirtIO, RDMA/RoCEv2, TCP/IP.
  • Strong programming proficiency in C, Python, and Linux shell scripting (Bash).
  • Micro-architectural understanding of modern CPU/ASIC memory hierarchies, PCIe Gen 5/6 interconnects, and Linux kernel networking stacks.
  • Proven track record using AI coding agents or automated script generators to streamline daily engineering workflows.

Ways to Stand Out from the crowd:

  • Deep hands-on experience tuning NVIDIA BlueField DPUs, ConnectX SmartNICs, or custom hardware offload engines.
  • Mastery of the full SPDK & NVMe-oF (NVMe over Fabrics) storage stack over high-speed RDMA transport layers.
  • Comprehensive system-level understanding across x86 (Intel/AMD) and Arm architectures, PCIe topology, and GPUDirect Storage (GDS).
  • Proven experience isolating stragglers and tail latency in multi-tenant, cloud-scale environments.

title: Senior Data Scientist, Data Quality and AI Evaluation
descriptionHtml:
At NVIDIA, we are building the next generation AI-native autonomous driving architecture — combining classical safety stacks, foundation models, and scalable AI systems into a unified production platform. Autonomous driving is entering a new era. Future AV systems will not be purely classical robotics stacks, nor purely end-to-end neural networks. The future lies in the deep integration of classical safety architectures and large-scale AI-driven systems. If you want to work on problems that build the future of autonomous systems over the next decade, this is the place.


What You’ll Be Doing

  • Define quality metrics and evaluation methods that reveal where auto-labeling pipelines succeed, fail, or regress.
  • Build and maintain human-verified golden datasets covering representative driving conditions, critical corner cases, historical failures, and new requirements.
  • Analyze large-scale sensor, camera and annotation data to identify root causes, discover systematic errors, and prioritize improvements with perception and auto-labeling engineers.
  • Develop automated approaches for failure clustering, similar-case discovery, and targeted selection of data for human correction.
  • Build statistically sound audits and experiments, establish release acceptance criteria, and communicate findings through clear dashboards and recommendations.
  • Partner with labeling operations to improve annotation guidelines, reviewer consistency, and the balance between quality, efficiency, and cost.

What We Need To See

  • Great foundations in statistics, experimental design, sampling, hypothesis testing, and uncertainty estimation, with practical experience evaluating machine learning systems and data quality.
  • Experience working on AI/LLM evaluation with proficiency in Python and SQL, including analyzing large datasets and building reproducible analytical workflows. Understanding of precision, recall, class imbalance, selection bias, data leakage, and evaluation across significant scenario groups.
  • Ability to distinguish reference-label defects from model errors and translate ambiguous quality concerns into measurable questions and actionable recommendations.
  • Strong communication and teamwork skills, with experience working across engineering, research, product, or operations teams.
  • 12+ years of industry experience with Bachelor degree or proven track record for Master in statistics, mathematics, computer science, engineering, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent experience in practice.

Ways To Stand Out from the Crowd:

  • Background with autonomous driving, robotics, or computer vision, particularly camera and LiDAR data, 2D/3D annotations, multi-object tracking, occupancy, or temporal and cross-sensor consistency.
  • Experience designing human-in-the-loop labeling and audit workflows, measuring annotator agreement, or maintaining versioned benchmarks with protected evaluation sets.

title: Senior Software Engineer – Platform and Deployability
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is powering the world’s most advanced AI Factories. Keeping them running depends on NVIDIA’s AI Ops platform for large-scale AI infrastructure — continuously ingesting telemetry from GPUs, NICs, switches, and links across the fleet, and delivered both as a high-scale SaaS service and as self-contained on-premises software for enterprise customers.


We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help make this platform deployable, operable, and scalable across customer-controlled environments ranging from a single node to tens of thousands of GPUs. This role sits at the intersection of platform software and runtime reality: packaging, configuration, deployment automation, upgrades, survivability, and large-scale operational correctness.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Build the deployment platform underneath the product: packaging, configuration, environment validation, upgrade paths, rollback flows, and runtime safeguards.
  • Own deployability across Kubernetes, cloud, on-prem, and restricted or air-gapped environments.
  • Design and improve the mechanisms that make the system installable and supportable at scale: Helm charts, deployment manifests, configuration schemas, dependency validation, readiness checks, and operational tooling.
  • Partner with backend and feature teams to ensure services are production-ready on day 1 and still correct on day 400.
  • Improve platform resilience: design for partial failure, misconfiguration, restarts, state loss, and degraded environments.
  • Turn scale and benchmark findings into concrete deployment guidance, sizing recommendations, and supported topologies.
  • Help evolve the platform from legacy deployment models toward a modern Kubernetes-based operational model.

What we need to see:

  • B.Sc. or M.Sc. in n Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field (Courses, Eligibility, Fees & Verified Programs), or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5+ years of software engineering experience in platform, infrastructure, runtime, or deployability-focused roles.
  • Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and production deployment tooling such as Helm, operators, or GitOps workflows.
  • Strong programming and automation skills in one or more of Go, Python, Bash, or similar.

  • Strong debugging skills across Linux, networking, containers, and service runtime behavior.
  • Experience with CI/CD, release engineering, environment validation, or infrastructure-as-code.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience delivering software into on-prem, customer-controlled, or air-gapped environments.

title: Senior CPU Power Architect
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a skilled CPU Power Architect to drive and optimize CPU power efficiency across the entire design cycle, from early architectural modeling through RTL implementation to silicon validation! In this role, you will work closely with software, architecture, RTL, physical design, and validation teams to identify power-saving opportunities, guide key design trade-offs, and ensure our CPUs achieve aggressive performance-per-watt goals. You will apply strong technical expertise in power analysis, modeling, and optimization while using silicon data to validate assumptions and refine future designs. Success in this position also requires excellent communication and collaboration skills, enabling you to influence cross-functional teams and help deliver highly efficient CPU products.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Pre-silicon Power Estimation: Model and estimate CPU power at C-model, RTL, and netlist stages using industry-standard tools.
  • Power Optimization: Identify inefficiencies and drive design improvements in collaboration with architects, RTL designers, and PD engineers.
  • Test Development: Create targeted power characterization tests (e.g., peak power, di/dt stress patterns) for both simulation and silicon.
  • Silicon Validation: Set up power measurement equipment and measure CPU power and performance in the lab; correlate silicon results with pre-silicon estimate to refine models.
  • Cross-functional Collaboration: Partner with multiple engineering disciplines to achieve optimal power efficiency without compromising performance.

What we need to see:

  • BS/MS in EE, CE, or CS or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years of experience working in ASIC power measurement and optimization.
  • Strong understanding of leakage and dynamic power in VLSI circuits.
  • Experience with RTL and netlist power analysis tools such as Power Artist, PrimeTime PX, or equivalent.
  • Familiarity with CPU microarchitecture and its impact on power (CPU pipeline design, out-of-order execution, cache hierarchy, branch prediction).

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Proficiency in using AI tools for automation and data analysis.
  • Experience with DVFS, clock gating, power gating, and multi-voltage domain design.
  • Knowledge of lab instrumentation for power measurement.
  • Strong communication skills for cross-team technical discussions.

NVIDIA is a global leader in accelerated computing, delivering breakthroughs in AI, HPC, and advanced system design. Our technologies power transformative applications across industries — from robotics and autonomous vehicles to healthcare and climate research.


With the introduction of the Grace and Vera CPU Superchips, NVIDIA has expanded into the CPU server market, complementing our world-class GPUs and SoCs. These CPUs play a critical role in orchestrating complex workloads with exceptional performance-per-watt efficiency. The CPU architecture team is driving innovations that integrate seamlessly with NVIDIA’s broader technology stack, enabling faster AI model training, efficient data processing, and scalable cloud deployments.

title: Deep Learning Compiler Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work.


We are building the next generation of compiler technologies to accelerate deep learning workloads. We are looking for an engineer to implement compiler verification software & related infrastructure in the AI space. You will be solving critical problems working alongside a diverse set of minds in GPU computing and systems software, doing what you enjoy. If this sounds like a fun challenge, we want to hear from you.


What you'll be doing:

  • Develop and maintain components of systems to reason about correctness in deep learning compilers, across graph transformations, IR lowering, and GPU execution.
  • Work with deep learning compiler and architecture teams to analyze and validate optimizations (e.g., graph rewrites in MLIR, fusion passes, mixed-precision transformations), ensuring they preserve semantics and numerical behavior.
  • Implement and extend test generation systems that use deep learning solutions and analysis methods to drive in-depth testing. These systems explore the vast combinatorial space of model topologies, precision modes, and hardware targets.
  • Contribute to improving how we measure functional quality and performance as models, compiler stacks, and hardware continue to evolve.

What we need to see:

  • BS, MS or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Mathematics, or equivalent experience.
  • 2+ years of hands-on software engineering experience, with experience in compiler development, deep learning systems, or compiler verification.
  • Proficiency in Python or C++ and experience with one major DL framework. This could be PyTorch, JAX/XLA, TensorRT, or a similar framework. Experience should involve model execution, graph representation, or runtime behavior.
  • Strong problem-solving and debugging skills — ability to reason about model behavior and compiler-generated code, investigate correctness issues, and collaborate with teammates to resolve edge-case failures.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience with compiler technologies such as LLVM, MLIR, TVM, or XLA, and familiarity with compiler passes, IR semantics, or correctness testing.
  • Exposure to formal methods or language specification: type systems, program semantics, or proof-based verification.
  • Experience with DL model internals such as quantization, operator fusion, mixed-precision, or graph-level optimization.

title: Software Engineer, Data Systems
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.


NVIDIA is seeking a Software Engineer, Data Systems to join our Santa Clara, CA team. This opportunity lets you work with innovative technology that changes how we analyze AI workload performance across GPU data centers. Our team builds advanced software tools to help technical users understand complex computing systems. You will manage the store, data model, and query path, converting large streams of profiling and telemetry data into useful information for engineers and automated analysis.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Develop and construct the store, data model, and query path for engineering performance data. This includes ingesting, joining, storing, and delivering it at the scale of a GPU data center with low latency.
  • Join profiling data with context from the rest of the system, such as hosts, schedulers, configuration, logs, and storage, ensuring each record carries the necessary identity and dimensions for comparison across jobs, machines, versions, and time.
  • Take responsibility for the data contract with the teams that generate the data: establish it, version it, and transition consumers through changes without disrupting them.
  • Make deliberate trade-offs among data quality, query latency, storage cost, and retention, and verify improvements in efficiency, latency, and resource use with measurements.
  • Handle delayed, duplicated, incomplete, or inconsistent data, and make its limitations visible to downstream users.
  • Develop the data API along with the generated evidence views for people and automated analysis to access results. Implement access controls, resource limits, and maintain stable behavior during high demand or failures.

What we need to see:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 12+ years of relevant software engineering experience, including delivery and operation of data pipelines, storage systems, analytical services, or comparable software used by others.
  • Experience handling large-scale data in production, including billions of events per day or petabyte-class stores. Also experienced with low-latency streaming pipelines that manage backpressure, replay, and duplicate delivery accurately.
  • Good judgment about event identity and ordering, data transformations, and how errors or missing data affect results.
  • A concrete performance investigation you can explain: the baseline, measurements, competing explanations, change made, and verified result, including trade-offs.
  • Experience establishing and versioning a data contract with a producing team, and guiding consumers through a format change.
  • Ability to debug across component boundaries and validate changes through code review, tests, and independent measurements, including when using automated development tools.
  • Clear communication about choices in building, observed behavior, and uncertainty, with care for users’ data and operational constraints.
  • Proficiency with C++, Python, and SQL.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Hands-on work with telemetry, time-series data, or analytical query engines such as ClickHouse, and with columnar formats such as Arrow and Parquet.
  • Familiarity with profiler data: trace record formats, sampling semantics, symbolization, clock domains, and aligning events recorded on different machines.
  • High-cardinality schema build, and measured improvements to memory use, storage efficiency, or query performance while preserving correctness.
  • A track record of making data processing easier to inspect and recover when inputs change, traffic spikes, or failures occur.
  • Working knowledge of Go.

Join us at NVIDIA and be part of a team that is defining the next era of computing. Together, we can make a significant impact on the world!

title: Senior Software Engineer - Autonomous Vehicles
descriptionHtml:
Self-driving cars need to detect the road’s course instantly, without relying on prior maps. We build an online mapping system that transforms raw sensor data into an accurate, live 3D model. This model shows lanes, boundaries, crosswalks, intersection structure, and traffic control semantics that the driving stack depends on. This is a software engineering role is central to that system. The algorithms are only as good as the software that runs them, so we need an engineer who obsesses over quality, performance, and architecture, and who can turn algorithmic ideas into safe, fast, maintainable code that runs in production vehicles on NVIDIA DRIVE Orin and Thor. The software you write will meet ASIL-B/D requirements and ship across L2++, L3, and L4 programs. You won’t be developing the algorithms from scratch, but you’ll need a strong grasp of them. You’ll work closely alongside algorithm engineers, and you need to understand what the code is doing to implement, optimize, and test it well.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Build and own core online mapping software operating in the car, from architecture through implementation to deployment.
  • Write production C++ for real-time embedded systems, with a focus on correctness, determinism, and maintainability.
  • Build software architecture and frameworks that promote code reuse, clean interfaces, and long-term maintainability across vehicle programs.
  • Improve performance of C++ and CUDA code running on NVIDIA DRIVE Orin and Thor, employing profilers to detect and address bottlenecks and to meet real-time budgets.
  • Use GPU parallelism (CUDA) to make compute-heavy mapping components fast and efficient.
  • Implement and incorporate algorithmic solutions from the mapping team into the core of NVIDIA’s AV stack, collaborating with algorithm engineers to understand and improve them.
  • Develop according to automotive safety standards (ASIL-B/D). Employ thorough static analysis and adhere to coding guidelines committed to safety. Reach 100% line and branch coverage through detailed unit and integration tests.
  • Handle real-time system signals from vehicles operating around the world, building software that is robust to varied conditions and failure modes.
  • Collaborate with perception, localization, planning, and infrastructure groups to incorporate online mapping into the complete AV stack across L2++, L3, and L4 programs.

What we need to see:

  • BS or MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years of validated experience building robust, production-quality software.
  • 3+ years of professional C++ development experience, including modern C++ and a strong grasp of memory management, concurrency, and performance.
  • Experience designing software architecture and APIs for large, long-lived codebases.
  • A quality-first mentality: comfortable with static analysis, unit testing, and high-coverage test strategies.
  • Solid understanding of algorithms and data structures, and the ability to work with algorithm developers and understand their work.
  • Strong communication and analytical skills, and the ability to work optimally across multiple teams.
  • Autonomous and responsible, demonstrating outstanding teamwork while enjoying solving hard problems.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Software development on embedded, real-time, or automotive platforms, including experience with real-time operating systems (e.g., QNX, Linux RT).
  • Experience with functional safety standards and processes (ISO 26262, ASIL-B/D), MISRA or AUTOSAR C++ coding guidelines, and safety-qualified toolchains.
  • Experience achieving high or full structural coverage (line and branch, ideally MC/DC) on production code.
  • Experience with GPGPU programming (CUDA) and GPU performance tuning.
  • Strong skills in runtime profiling and optimization of CPU and GPU code.

title: Senior Compiler Engineer – Rust GPU
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is dedicated to reinvent accelerated computing. Reinvention requires great technology and amazing people. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

NVIDIA is hiring a Senior Compiler Engineer to join our team driving the next generation of GPU systems programming. We are redefining how developers write high-performance GPU software by bringing the safety, expressiveness, and modern tooling of Rust to native GPU and CUDA development. On this team, you will build cutting-edge compiler pipelines, custom intermediate representation (IR) frameworks, and JIT compilation systems that bridge host and device execution—allowing developers to write memory-safe, high-performance GPU kernels in idiomatic Rust.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Develop Rust-to-GPU Compiler Pipelines: Design, implement, and maintain custom compiler backends (such as rustc codegen backends and proc-macros) and Rust-native intermediate representation (IR) frameworks to compile standard Rust directly to high-performance CUDA PTX and machine code.

  • Build compiler IRs and Optimizers: Work with modern compiler architectures to lower Rust AST and MIR into IRs including MLIR, PTX, and LLVM, including GPU-specific optimizations.

  • Support complex ahead-of-time, just-in-time, and link time optimization workflows: Build state-of-the-art tooling to support users targeting a broad family of NVIDIA GPUs, host platforms, and feature sets.

  • Define Safe Parallel Abstractions: Architect innovative compiler-enforced safety models that extend Rust's ownership, borrowing, and lifetime disciplines across the GPU launch boundary—preventing data races and enforcing memory safety during asynchronous GPU execution.

  • Expose Next-Gen Hardware Features: Implement type-safe, ergonomic device-side abstractions in Rust for low-level GPU hardware primitives, including shared memory, barriers, scoped atomics, Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA), and warp/cluster-level operations.

  • Build the future: Supporting today’s accelerated computing applications is not sufficient. We have to build composable building blocks for others around us to build the applications of tomorrow.

What we need to see:

  • Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • 5+ years of relevant work or research experience in compiler development, language design, or GPU code generation.

  • Deep expertise in the Rust programming language, including a strong grasp of compiler internals (rustc), Rust MIR, procedural macros, and Rust's borrow-checker/lifetime model.

  • Hands-on experience with compiler infrastructures, intermediate representations (IRs), and code generation (such as LLVM IR, MLIR, or custom IR systems).

  • Solid understanding of parallel programming models, GPU architectures, and CUDA programming.

  • Strong software design skills, including debugging, profiling, and benchmarking compilers and GPU kernels.

  • Ability to orchestrate agents for product requirement design, architecture, code development, testing, code review, and issue triage.

  • Ability to work independently, define project goals and scope, and drive complex compiler-engineering efforts from research to production.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • A track record of contributing to the Rust compiler (rustc), Cargo tooling, or open-source Rust-to-GPU projects.

  • Experience building custom compiler front-ends, AST translators, or JIT engines.

  • Familiarity with MLIR or other extensible compiler frameworks.

  • Deep proficiency in low-level GPU programming, including the use of modern hardware features (e.g., Tensor Cores, warp-level shuffles, or asynchronous transfer pipelines).

  • Experience designing Domain-Specific Languages (DSLs) or tile-based programming abstractions for tensor processing.

title: Senior Mechanical Hardware Design Engineer, IC Product
descriptionHtml:

You will lead the mechanical design and execution of test hardware for NVIDIA’s networking and CPO (Co-Packaged Optics) products: test boards, sockets, handler interfaces, system-level test (SLT) mechanical interfaces, and HTOL platforms.

NVIDIA’s Networking division is a leading supplier of end-to-end InfiniBand and Ethernet connectivity solutions for data centers, including adapter cards, switches, cables and software. Our products deliver industry-leading bandwidth, performance and scalability. The IC PE HW team ensures these products are tested and qualified for high-volume production.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Design, define and qualify test sockets, contactors, handler change kits and thermal solutions for high-power, high-speed devices, with full ownership of the mechanical specification, mechanical component selection, and mechanical constraints for board layout (keep-out zones, placement, stiffening). Manage the external vendors who supply them, including drawing reviews and design sign-off.
  • Lead lab bring-up and debug, and define the thermal and mechanical constraints of test platforms so they deploy efficiently and robustly on the production floor, while meeting high-speed signal integrity requirements.
  • Work with the most advanced ATE platforms in the industry, including Teradyne UltraFLEX / UltraFLEXplus and Advantest V93K testers and probers.
  • Develop mechanical interfaces for optical systems on production ATE equipment, and define new design concepts for future CPO products.
  • Collaborate with R&D and Production teams: board design, system-level test, signal integrity, layout, firmware and test engineering.
  • Lead HTOL (High-Temperature Operating Life) hardware platforms for reliability testing.

What we need to see:

  • B.Sc. in Mechanical Engineering.
  • 5+ years of experience as a Mechanical Design Engineer, with hands-on 3D CAD (Creo preferred)
